messages.subject: Digikam issue
parts: I know it is not technically a camtrapR question, but has anyone had any issues with the digikam program not allowing you to import pictures? Every time I go to import my camera trap pictures into digikam to begin metadata tagging, it freezes the program. I initially thought it was because of the sheer amount of pictures,  however it does the same thing when I try to import a single picture. I assume a lot of you have used this program because it was suggested so I figured here is a good place to ask.

messages.author: a9b015cd2c9c75be
messages.subject: Re: Digikam issue
parts:
Hi,

I haven't had this problem with any of our work computers as far as I know. It might be a good idea to ask Gilles Caulier 

They have an online help forum which is very quick and thousands of people to reply:
> http://digikam.1695700.n4.nabble.com/digikam-users-f1735189.html

Or I think you can also try email the user list at:
> digika...@kde.org

I am not sure if you have done this already but if not make sure in the configuration settings of digikam that images are loaded at a reduced size. This doesn't change the quality that much and you will still be able to identify all the animals in the images but it makes digikam much faster and easier to run. So perhaps this is why digikam crashes/freezes. You can select this when you set up/install digikam. You can also select it if you click on the the top menu bar and scroll to configure digikam > Views > Preview > then select the one that says "Preview shows embedded view if available (faster)".

While you are in the configuration settings also make sure you have selected that the metadata be written to the image. This happened to me a long time ago - I had tagged about 200,000 photos and then when I wanted to extract the data, there was nothing... At that point I wanted to eat my computer! Go to: Metadata > Behaviour  and under "Write this Information to the Metadata" make sure "Image Tags" are selected.

Also, I usually don't upload more than 10,000-20,000 photos at a time and then just tag those first before I upload a new album and tag those, otherwise (depending on the type of computer) digikam can lag slightly. Also, I was told that it is better to upload images from a local drive instead of an external hard drive in digikam (especially for Mac OS apparently). 

Lastly, I know a new version 5.9.0 came out recently, might be a good start to also download this if you haven't already. The stable version 6.0.0 is also on it's way and beta version one is currently being tested for this one - so hopefully that will sort out your problem.

Lastly, lastly...Please reply when you figure out what the problem was. I am curious to know why your computer is freezing and what can be done to solve it. Thanks!

Good Luck,
Philip
